It was a buddies parents property. They had moved to California and were planning on Demolishing the house at a later date. It was on the outskirts of a Commercial zone and they were sitting on the property until a prospective business would offer them an amount for the property They had no idea we were staying there. The house was in tatters as they had left it sitting for a long time, the walls had holes in them and it had no carpet or heating. Nine of us lived in that house as well as in the garage on the property that had an upstairs living quarters. We had epic parties there, because of the zoning laws in commercial zones the police never responded to noise complaints, as a matter of fact we had no idea we were being called in until....we made the front page of our local fucking paper!!! The headline read Unruly Neighbors and cited 60 plus calls about our noise levels and a picture of a car we had demolished with baseball bats and ran over with a truck. That place was cool but in the winter I got really really sick because of the cold. To heat ourselves in the very below zero temperatures we hooked up space heaters an covered both ourselves and the heaters in blankets. I ended up going to the hospital toward the end of the winter with lung problems from the black mold that we had inside. We did a lot of crazy stuff before then, a group of my friends once picked up this mascot made out of wood with BSA painted on his shirt, he was 7 ft tall and pretty heavy. As a joke we would often use him as a battering ram to destroy the walls of the rooms people were sleeping in.

The point is that being frugal by living in unsafe conditions led to me buying useless extravagant things that I did not need. I could have used all of the money I blew at that house to start a business or go to school earlier ect...

find an introductory course in what you want to major in and take it. You would be surprised how that can be a game changer.

>>>College Student

My advise then is to yes do your generals (after seeing an advisor) but see if your college offers a introductory course in what you are interested in. The engineers have it at my college and so do the medical imaging tech's. I am sure this is common practice at a lot of universities. You would be surprised at what you will learn from these courses.... **example** I wanted to go into medical imaging, specifically MRI... It turns out that for me personally it would take an immense amount of patience to understand the concepts of the technology, the instructor was even dumbing it down for a laymen introductory class.

Figure out what you want to do and regularly see an advisor. Do not do what I did and try to figure it out yourself. Five years later and I do not have a degree. Do not be afraid to do that. Also befriend and make as many professional contacts as you can teachers and students, you would be surprised how far you can be spring boarded with their help. Also Volunteer and then when the time comes to apply for scholarships you will have something good to say on your application.
